title: node-health-breakfast-runbook
content:
Purpose: quick morning runbook for node/gpu health checks before standup. Personal scratchpad — shorthand, items to tick off, CLI snippets, follow-ups. Not official runbook, use for fast triage and handoff.

Top priorities (first 15m):
- glance at cluster-wide health dashboard (console -> infra > nodes) - look for red nodes or >2 pods in CrashLoop
- check GPU utilization anomalies (sustained 95% for >10m on >1 node)
- confirm no persistent OOMKilled pods in inference namespace
- ensure no recent node reboots outside scheduled window

Quick commands I run (copy-paste):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount
- kubectl top nodes --no-headers | sort -k3 -nr   # CPU/mem
- kubectl top pods -n inference | head -n 30
- ssh ops@node-XXX sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv,noheader,nounits
- sudo journalctl -u docker -n 200   # on node for recent daemon errors
- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:PORT/health | jq '.'  # local health check for sidecars

Thresholds / decision guide (my quick mental model):
- If GPU util >= 95% on 2+ nodes for >10m -> check recent batch jobs, look for runaway batch job label; consider scaling Dedicated pool or adding burst nodes. Open INF ticket if capacity shortage.
- If node reports NotReady -> SSH; check kubelet logs, docker; if kubelet OOM, cordon+drain and rotate. If kernel panic previously -> escalate SRE.
- If >5 pods OOMKilled in 10m -> possible memory regression in model binary; tag suspects and alert models team.

Current TODOs (personal):
- [ ] follow up with Jonah on infra-autoscaler anomaly from last night (notes in PR-879) — priority medium
- [ ] push small helper script to wrap nvidia-smi outputs into Prom format (save to tools/gpu-scrape) — low
- [ ] verify node-21 NIC flapping => check switch logs (contact network team if pattern repeats) — high
- [ ] add quick link to this doc in my oncall playbook (consolidate) — low

Notes from last night (things to remember):
- brief spike around 03:22 UTC, several inference pods retried once then recovered. Cause: transient EBS latency hitting model cache hot paths (ticket INF-3207). Configured fallback cache policy in canary; watch for regressions.
- scheduled maintenance for rack-6 next Tue 02:00-04:00 PT; remember to migrate long-running jobs.

Escalation contacts (quick):
- network: Priya S. (slack @priya), pager: PR-Dispatch-1
- sres: Jonah L. (oncall rotation pager)
- models: eng-models Slack, ping @Oliver for urgent model rollbacks

Common snippets I scribble here:
- drain and reprovision node quickly: kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force && ssh ops@NODE sudo reboot
- force-clear nv cache for cuda app: sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm || true; sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm || true  # be careful, requires restart of pods after

Open questions / follow-ups to capture before handoff:
- Did we correlate 03:22 spike to a specific customer job ID? (check logs: /var/log/inference/jobs.log)
- What's the plan for autoscaler warm pool sizing for upcoming demo on 2026-04-01? (action: schedule sync with Product)

Random quick wins to remember:
- Add short grep alias to ~/.bashrc: alias gpustats='ssh ops@%s sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv,noheader'
- Add alert: if node kernel messages include 'oom_reaper', page SRE immediately (OOM pattern seen twice in two months)

End-of-shift handoff checklist (if leaving early):
- leave open INF tickets assigned, add short comment with current state
- if any cordoned nodes, file a Jira for reprovision and label owner
- drop 1-line summary in #infra-ops with top 2 items and whether action required

Random notes-to-self (messy):
- check open PR-879 CI flakiness on staging; one test times out when gpu node under 80% mem but high GPU util -> could be race in test harness
- remind myself to remove temporary debug env var set on node-12 after reproducing memory leak

-- maya
